tool_input.body:
## The finding this PR is built on

Four of cluster 2's five bugs are **one defect**. `internal/mission` carries two storage layers — a per-repo tree and a flat global tree shared by every repo on the machine — and call sites choose between them inconsistently. Enumeration spans both. Locking uses one while the data lives in the other. Resolution uses only one.

So this starts with an ADR, **DES-075**, rather than four patches. Fixing the symptoms separately would have left the ambiguity that produced them.

**Decisions:** the repo tree is authoritative for new writes (already true) and now for the write-set conflict scan; the global tree stays a read-only fallback and is excluded from the scan; the repo-tier lock is authoritative for delegation-directory access; and a linked worktree's own `.punt-labs/ethos/` is named **inert**.

## Three beads recorded the wrong mechanism

Triage on 2026-09-07 corrected each, and this PR builds to the correction — not the original text.

| Bead | Filed cause | Actual cause |
|---|---|---|
| `ethos-6adb` | cwd resolution; fix via `--repo` flag | `Store.List()` enumerates the unscoped global tree |
| `ethos-lj4k` | `Abandon` runs unlocked | `Abandon` holds a *different lock file* |
| `ethos-7tqd` | orphaned contracts sit inert | orphans are **active** and capture the next agent spawn |

Both filed fixes were rejected in triage: the `--repo` flag targets a cwd resolution that isn't happening, and adding a second lock to `Abandon` invites a lock-ordering deadlock.

## Per bead

**`ethos-6adb`** — conflict scan scoped to the repo tree. Measured on one host: 841 contracts in the global tree, 19 open, and **zero carrying a `repo:` field** — so repo-filtering alone would fix nothing for existing data, which is why the global tree is excluded outright rather than filtered.

**`ethos-lj4k`** — `Abandon` now nests the repo-tier exclusive lock *inside* the existing global lock, matching the global→repo acquisition order `delegation.go`'s own doc comment already prescribed. Nested, not dual-independent, so no new deadlock risk.

The regression is the good part: it confirmed the race **live** before the fix — `Abandon` resolved successfully within 200ms while a `dispatchTierB`-shaped writer still held the repo-tier lock. Post-fix it blocks, then correctly refuses.

**`ethos-ouy9`** — `writeContract` and `restoreContract` now match `writeRoster`'s discipline: `Sync` before close, temp removed on every error path, failed fsync propagated. `Create` reads the contract back before returning nil. The two other candidate causes from triage (layer mismatch, cross-repo landing) are ruled out for any repo-scoped invocation by Decisions 1 and 2, independently of the fsync gap.

**`ethos-5yej`** — no code change, correctly. Resolving the repo layer to the main work tree is what lets a linked worktree see its parent's missions. The ADR now *names* the behaviour instead of leaving it silently undefined.

**`ethos-7tqd`** — partial, deliberately. `dispatch`/`create` now print the binding on every bind rather than only on rebinds, so the capture is at least visible. The better fixes — binding at worker-spawn time, and letting `abandon` clean up a mission whose only delegation is one it captured — both require `internal/hook/pretooluse_dispatch.go`, outside this mission's write-set. Left as a named follow-up rather than silently expanding scope.

That restraint is deliberate and worth noting: `ethos-73ht` records what happens when a leader widens scope by message without amending the contract — the worker is left choosing between an unfilable result and a dishonest one.

## Verification

Detached CI simulation — clean `git archive`, `setsid`, all `CLAUDE_*` stripped — run by implementer and leader independently: **27 ok / 0 FAIL / 1 no-test-files**.

`make check` green before every commit (4/4). `go test -race ./internal/mission/...` clean. `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` exits 0 — this package gained Windows locking in #507.

Every behavioural change has a regression **confirmed red before the fix**. One honest caveat, flagged by the implementer rather than glossed: `ouy9`'s read-back test was red pre-fix by non-compilation (the hooks don't exist there), not by a runtime failure. Stated rather than overclaimed.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

tool_input.message:
Pushed. PR #508 is open. I verified independently before pushing rather than taking the report: DES-075 present at DESIGN.md:8894, `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` exit 0, and the detached gate under my own setsid run at 27 ok / 0 FAIL — matching yours exactly.

YOUR SCOPE PUSHBACK IS UPHELD, and it is the right call for a reason beyond the write-set boundary itself.

You stopped because binding-at-spawn and abandon-cleanup both need `internal/hook/pretooluse_dispatch.go`, outside your write_set, and you refused to widen it unilaterally. That is exactly the trap `ethos-73ht` records: earlier today I expanded a mission by message without amending its contract, and `mission result --verify` then refused the worker's honest `files_changed` — leaving it to choose between an unfilable result and a dishonest one. It escalated correctly and the mission still carries a permanent `verdict: escalate` for a bookkeeping reason. There is no `ethos mission amend`, so I cannot widen yours either. Folding internal/hook into this branch would reproduce that failure exactly.

So: the 7tqd remainder gets its own mission with the right write_set from the start. Your in-scope third option — printing the binding on every bind — is the correct partial, because it makes the capture visible immediately rather than leaving it silent while the real fix waits.

Three things in your report I want to name:

The lj4k regression is the best test written in this repo today. It confirmed the race LIVE — Abandon resolving within 200ms while a dispatchTierB-shaped writer still held the repo-tier lock — rather than asserting the fix's shape. That is a test that would have caught the bug had it existed, which is the only kind worth having.

Nesting inside the existing global lock, in the order delegation.go's own doc comment already prescribed, instead of taking two independent locks. I flagged the deadlock risk in the triage note; you found the ordering was already documented and followed it. Better than what I asked for.

And you flagged that ouy9's read-back test was red pre-fix by NON-COMPILATION rather than a runtime failure, instead of letting "confirmed red" stand unqualified. That distinction is real and most reports would have skipped it. It went into the PR description verbatim.

One question before I close the mission, and I want your read rather than a yes: DES-075 Decision 5 names a worktree's own `.punt-labs/ethos/` as inert. ethos-5yej's whole complaint is that this is silent. Does the ADR text alone satisfy that, or should something at runtime say so — a doctor check, or a warning when `ethos enable` deposits into a linked worktree whose main tree has no store? I lean toward the latter being a separate bead rather than a blocker, but you have read the code more recently than I have.

Stand by for review findings on #508 — expect several; this PR touches locking and durability, and the last two PRs drew nine and five.

tool_input.content: My read: doctor check, not an enable-time warning…
tool_input.message:
My read: doctor check, not an enable-time warning, and yes — a separate bead, not a blocker.

Reasoning: the ADR text alone documents the behavior but doesn't detect the bad state. An enable-time warning only fires the moment someone runs `ethos enable` in a worktree — it misses every other way to reach the same trap (a worktree created after the main tree's store already existed, or a worktree whose `.punt-labs/ethos/` picked up content some other way, with `enable` never re-run there). A doctor check fires on demand regardless of how the state arose, which matches how `ethos doctor` already treats this exact repoRoot-vs-storeRoot distinction — `CheckOrphanedAgentFiles(repoRoot, storeRoot, ...)` in internal/doctor/doctor.go is already built around "these two differ inside a linked worktree" (its own doc comment says so, citing the Bugbot #370 class). A new check slots into that same, already-established pattern rather than inventing a new one.

Concretely: compare `resolve.FindRepoRoot()` (this checkout) against `resolve.StoreRepoRoot()` (main tree); if they differ and `<repoRoot>/.punt-labs/ethos/` exists with real content, WARN that it's inert and content lives in storeRoot instead — same shape as the existing check, same file. Small, additive, no change to enable or resolve's actual behavior. I did not implement this — it's outside m-2026-09-08-001's write_set and you're already closing that mission — but it's a clean, well-scoped follow-up bead if you want to file it now rather than let it drift.
